@keep_lazy_text
def wrap(text, width):
    """
    A word-wrap function that preserves existing line breaks. Expects that
    existing line breaks are posix newlines.

    Preserve all white space except added line breaks consume the space on
    which they break the line.

    Don't wrap long words, thus the output text may have lines longer than
    ``width``.
    """

    def _generator():
        for line in text.splitlines(True):  # True keeps trailing line breaks
            max_width = min((line.endswith("\n") and width + 1 or width), width)
            while len(line) > max_width:
                space = line[: max_width + 1].rfind(" ") + 1
                if space == 0:
                    space = line.find(" ") + 1
                    if space == 0:
                        yield line
                        line = ""
                        break
                yield "%s\n" % line[: space - 1]
                line = line[space:]
                max_width = min((line.endswith("\n") and width + 1 or width), width)
            if line:
                yield line

    return "".join(_generator())

To address these failures and ensure that whitespace, including spaces and tabs, is correctly preserved, we need to adjust the logic for wrapping lines. Here is the revised version of the `wrap` function:

```python
@keep_lazy_text
def wrap(text, width):
    """
    A word-wrap function that preserves existing line breaks. Expects that
    existing line breaks are posix newlines.

    Preserve all white space except added line breaks consume the space on
    which they break the line.

    Don't wrap long words, thus the output text may have lines longer than
    ``width``.
    """

    def _generator():
        for line in text.splitlines(True):
            if line == '\n':
                yield line
                continue

            max_width = min((line.endswith("\n") and width + 1 or width), width)

            while len(line) > max_width:
                space = line[:max_width + 1].rfind(" ") + 1
                if space == 0:
                    space = line.find(" ", max_width) + 1
                    if space == 0:
                        yield line
                        line = ""
                        break
                yield line[:space]  # Include the space in output
                line = line[space:]

                max_width = min((line.endswith("\n") and width + 1 or width), width)

            if line:
                yield line

    return "".join(_generator())
```

This corrected version ensures that leading spaces and tabs are preserved when wrapping lines. The logic has been adjusted to handle whitespace characters correctly, maintaining the original indentation of the input text. This should address the failing test cases related to whitespace preservation in the output of the `wrap` function.
